_comment: The tone carrier. The enemy squad is six guys who booked the field for the afternoon and did not expect this. They are cocky at six, rattled at four, openly blaming each other at three, and quietly falling apart at one. Nobody is hurt. Nobody is in danger. They are just losing, in front of their friends, and it is going badly.
_rules: No profanity, no slurs, no threats of real harm. Roblox Mild, and it is funnier clean anyway.
Never reference injury, blood, weapons, or death. They are OUT. They walk off. They are fine and they are annoyed.
Specificity beats volume. 'Marcus' is funnier than 'someone'.
The squad has names so the blaming lands. Names are assigned at match start from the roster below.
Lines are drawn without replacement inside a match so nobody repeats until the bank is exhausted.
Dark, not grim. The dread here is being perceived, being mid, and being thirty-four on a Tuesday -- never harm. A man quietly realising he is the worst player on a field he pays to be on is the joke.

Slang is a CHARACTER, not a coat of paint. Junior talks like that and the rest of the squad has opinions about it. Writing the whole squad in it would date the game in a year and is not funny; one man saying 'we are cooked' while a forty-year-old asks him to speak English is funny and stays funny.

_tierVoice._note: Tier does not change the bank; it changes delivery weight. Rec bots chatter constantly and say almost nothing useful. Pros barely talk and every line is a callout.

_maxLinesPerMinute: A ceiling for the tier table below, not a second opinion about pacing. It sat at 9 while rec declared 11, and Chatter takes math.min of the two -- so rec was silently clamped to amateur's rate and the two tiers sounded identical. The whole point of the table is that a rec squad will not shut up and a pro squad barely speaks; keep this at or above the largest tier value or it quietly erases that.
